clue.text: Deceitful twin daughter that's drunk ale and gin

parts.note: a twin is a double, an exact copy

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of ale and gin are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: A treacherous twin's daughter has been downing ale and gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like it describes the daughter, but it is the signal to rearrange the drinks; EALING is a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-dealing is duplicity, behaviour that is two-faced and deceitful, so the adjective form is a synonym.

clue.text: Besotted with bad liar, so what shall we do with him?

definitions.text: what shall we do with him?

parts.note: besotted can mean stupefied with drink, intoxicated

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of liar and so are spoilt into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A lovestruck dupe is infatuated with a terrible fibber, and someone asks what to do with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges LIAR and SO into SAILOR. The definition quotes the sea shanty 'What shall we do with the drunken sailor?'
explanation.definitionFit: The famous shanty asks this very question about its hero, so the line serves as an allusive definition.

clue.text: Men into nudes represented as detached by Turner?

indicators.note: into signals that one piece goes inside the other
represented suggests the letters of nudes are presented again in a different order

parts.note: a crew is a team of men, as on a ship

explanation.surface: An art critic suggests that putting men among nudes was the painter Turner's way of showing detachment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' signals the rearrangement of the nudes. 'Turner' is not the painter J. M. W. Turner but a screwdriver, a thing that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken off by a screwdriver, a tool that turns, has been unfastened, a whimsical cryptic definition.

clue.text: City hospital has adjoining houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the answer sits inside the words hospital has adjoining

explanation.surface: A city hospital has neighbouring houses beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun next to 'adjoining', but it is the verb that hides the answer across the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital city of Tibet, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Profound quality of positive note found in two letters

indicators.note: found in signals that one piece is located inside another

parts.note: the two letters are D and S, each spelt out as a word, side by side

explanation.surface: A profound positive note turns up in a couple of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters of the alphabet can be clued by their spelt-out names, here dee and ess; 'found in' puts the positive note between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth of thought or feeling is a profound quality, which the noun names directly as a synonym.

clue.text: A milkman's way of moving out of debt

parts.note: a milk float is the small electric van used by British milkmen on their rounds

explanation.surface: A milkman's mode of transport is presented as the route to financial solvency.
explanation.walkthrough: A milk float is the slow electric delivery cart of British milkmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Being afloat financially means staying solvent, keeping clear of debt, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Establishment providing home for former partner in special case

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so home substitutes for the former partner within the word

parts.note: an exception is a special case outside the rule
an ex is a former partner
in means at home

explanation.surface: An institution provides a home for an ex-partner as a special case.
explanation.walkthrough: In EXCEPTION, IN takes the place of EX.
explanation.definitionFit: The inception of something is its founding or beginning, the same as its establishment.

clue.text: Drunken topless binge in which one's drunk spirits

indicators.note: drunk means swallowed, so the result takes one inside it
drunken suggests the remaining letters stagger into a new order
topless means the first letter of binge is removed

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A wild binge with the tops off where somebody has had too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts BINGE to INGE; 'Drunken' rearranges that to GENI, and 'drunk' (swallowed) takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genie, a magical spirit of Arabian folklore, so the word means spirits.

clue.text: Drop scone in whisky, then slag off bar

parts.note: Scotch is whisky made in Scotland
to slag off is British slang for criticise harshly, as is to pan
a cake can be a bar, as in a cake of soap

explanation.surface: Someone dunks a scone in whisky, then bad-mouths the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slag off' is British slang for criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop scone is a small thick griddle pancake made by dropping batter onto a hot plate, also called a Scotch pancake.

clue.text: Firm delivering to gallery north of New York?

parts.note: UPS is the American parcel delivery company
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A courier company sends a package to an art gallery in northern New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstate New York is the part of the state lying north of New York City, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Nicola Charles's first acting brief

indicators.note: acting suggests the letters are performing a new role, rearranged
first picks out the opening letter of Charles

explanation.surface: Nicola and Charles are in a short theatre engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acting' rearranges NICOLA plus C.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, so it is terse, short or brief.

clue.text: Fate of soul with a jolly heart

indicators.note: heart puts the jolly at the centre of the other letters

parts.note: the ka is the soul or spirit in ancient Egyptian belief
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: The destiny of a happy-hearted soul.
explanation.walkthrough: KA plus A has RM put at its heart. 'Jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Karma in Hindu and Buddhist thought is the destiny one's deeds bring, hence fate.

clue.text: One can't focus any closer than this part in one's play

definitions.text: One can't focus any closer than this

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are being toyed with into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A part in someone's play is the limit of their focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges the letters of PART IN ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The near point is the closest distance at which the eye can see an object sharply.

clue.text: Foursome playing game with actors in TV programme?

parts.note: the four bridge players are North, East, West and South
the actors in a production are its cast

explanation.surface: Four people play a game with actors on a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge the players are named for compass points: N, E, W, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A newscast is a broadcast of the news, a kind of television programme.

clue.text: Helping one to get rid of rocking chair, with tact needed

definitions.text: Helping one to get rid of

indicators.note: rocking shakes the letters of chair and tact into another order

explanation.surface: Someone needs tact while helping dispose of a rocking chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocking' looks like it describes the chair, but it rearranges CHAIR and TACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cathartic purges, helping a person release pent-up feelings, hence helping one to get rid of them.

clue.text: Angle enclosing home end

indicators.note: enclosing means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
in means at home

explanation.surface: An angle surrounding a house's end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angle' looks like a noun but is the verb, to fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A finish is the conclusion or end of something, a straight synonym.

clue.text: First person in Germany to name 28 countries with second name for "mongoose"

parts.note: ich is German for I, the first person pronoun
N again for name
the European Union had 28 member states at the time
mo is a moment, a second
N again for name

explanation.surface: A German introduces himself to a list of nations, offering a second name for the mongoose.
explanation.walkthrough: The EU had 28 members before Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ichneumon is the Egyptian mongoose, so it is another name for that animal.

clue.text: Notice mirror in telescope

parts.note: to spy is to catch sight of, notice
a glass is a looking glass, a mirror

explanation.surface: Someone spots a mirror inside a telescope.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small hand-held telescope, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Composed second note to lawyer before trial even starts

indicators.note: before places the lawyer ahead of the starting letters

parts.note: E is a musical note
a DA is an American district attorney

indicators.note: starts takes the first letter of trial and of even

explanation.surface: A calm second note is passed to a lawyer before the trial gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' is not 'even so': with 'trial' it gives the opening letters T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sedate is calm and unhurried, the same as composed.

clue.text: See 1
Kind of workplace in Sweden, into free dance

indicators.note: into puts Sweden inside the other pieces

parts.note: open means free, unrestricted
a hop is an informal dance
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: A Swedish workplace has broken out into a free-form dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the insertion; S is Sweden's international vehicle registration code.
explanation.definitionFit: An open shop is a workplace where employees need not belong to a trade union.

clue.text: See 8
Wild stab, making piano loud

indicators.note: making here means turning one into the other, so piano becomes loud

parts.note: to pierce is to stab
P is the musical marking for piano, softly
F is forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A musician makes a wild attempt at playing a quiet passage loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano) in PIERCE changes to F (forte).
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce means savage or ferocious, as a wild animal is.

clue.text: Cutting off current, it's a long shot

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters of it's a long are rearranged

explanation.surface: An electrician cuts off the power, thinking it's a long shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long shot' looks like a phrase, but 'shot' rearranges ITS ALONG into SOLATING, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolating something cuts it off or separates it from others, as in isolating a circuit.

clue.text: Ask for fringe to be shortened initially

indicators.note: shortened initially means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a border is a fringe or edge

explanation.surface: A customer at the hairdresser asks for the fringe to be trimmed first.
explanation.walkthrough: BORDER drops its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To order something is to request it, as in a restaurant, so the verb means ask for.

clue.text: Antarctic explorer in film as miscreant

indicators.note: the explorer in film makes the word miscreant, so taking the film away leaves the explorer

parts.note: this is a coincidence of position only: the film is split around the explorer, three letters before and one after, so the device is taking a container away
a mist is a thin film, as of condensation

explanation.surface: A polar explorer is portrayed in a movie as a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie, but it is MIST: put the explorer in MIST and you get MISCREANT, so removing MIST from that word leaves him.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Crean was an Irish seaman who went on Scott's and Shackleton's Antarctic expeditions.

clue.text: Hide one member of raccoon family

parts.note: an animal's hide is its coat
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: One member of the raccoon family goes into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted American mammal of the raccoon family Procyonidae.

clue.text: Person getting on train read lots, but no article

indicators.note: to train is to direct or shape, so the letters are formed into a new order
but no means the article is left out

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An elderly person on a train reads plenty, but no newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on' looks like boarding the train, but it means ageing. READ LOTS loses A, and 'train' rearranges REDLOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an elderly person, someone who is getting on in years.

clue.text: A man that is sick, with a blood deficiency

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters are in a bad way, rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is unwell because he is short of blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' signals the rearrangement of A MAN together with the abbreviation for 'that is'; the second 'a' is added unchanged at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia is a lack of red blood cells or haemoglobin, a deficiency of the blood.

clue.text: Eccentric old English king, upset about son? That's a very tricky subject!

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the son
upset knocks the letters over into a new arrangement

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A dotty old English king is upset about his son, which is no easy topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like it describes the king, but it is fodder; 'upset' rearranges ECCENTRIC with OE and K, and 'about' wraps that round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocket science is used idiomatically for anything fiendishly difficult, as in 'it's not rocket science'.
